investigation_authority: Bureau d'enquêtes sur les événements de mer (BEA mer)
participating_administrations: Direzione Generale per le Investigazioni Ferroviarie e Marittime (DIGIFEMA, Italy)
Ministère du Transport / Direction Générale des Transports Maritimes (Tunisia)
report_title: Rapport d'enquête technique: Abordage survenu le 7 octobre 2018 entre le roulier Ulysse et le porte-conteneurs CSL Virginia
incident_classification: Very Serious Marine Casualty (Pollution & Severe Structural Damage)

incident_event.location: International waters, approximately 15 nautical miles north of Cap Corse, Corsica, France

meteorological_conditions_at_impact.sea_state: Slight (Douglas state 2, wave height 0.5 to 1.25 m)
meteorological_conditions_at_impact.current: Liguro-Provençal (Northern) surface current flowing west-southwest (~0.2 to 0.4 knots)

navigation_data_at_collision.radar_status: S-band radar operating; target CSL Virginia acquired automatically at 04:53 UTC with CPA=0
navigation_data_at_collision.bridge_manning: Single officer of watch on bridge, inattentive due to personal telephone call behind chart table curtains

navigation_data_at_collision.bridge_watch: Anchor watch maintained on bridge; radar operating but inattention to closing collision risk

impact_and_damage.geometry: Perpendicular impact into starboard side of CSL Virginia between cargo bays 22 and 26
impact_and_damage.hull_breach: Rupture of CSL Virginia starboard fuel bunker Tank #3 (capacity 1,376 m³)
impact_and_damage.structural_consequence: Vessels locked tightly together for 4 days until separation on 2018-10-11

pollution_ground_truth.pollutant_type: IFO 380 (Intermediate Fuel Oil / Heavy Bunker Fuel)

observed_slick_characteristics.satellite_radar_detection: Sentinel-1A SAR pass on 2018-10-08 05:28:07 UTC clearly imaged continuous plume emanating from the entangled vessels.
observed_slick_characteristics.coastal_impact: Oil patties beached along the French Var coast (Pampelonne, Saint-Tropez, Sainte-Maxime, Ramatuelle) between October 16 and 18, 2018.

investigation_conclusions.primary_cause: Critical lack of proper lookout on board ULYSSE under Rule 5 of COLREGs due to personal mobile phone distraction by officer of watch.
investigation_conclusions.secondary_cause: Imprudent anchoring location of CSL VIRGINIA in high-density merchant transit approach to Corsica Channel TSS, combined with ineffective anchor-watch collision risk assessment.
investigation_conclusions.mechanical_failures: None. All propulsion, steering, radar, and navigation systems on both vessels were operational.
